records.supported_name_scope: The selected mainstem begins on Río Tigre west of Lago Cholila and crosses the connected Cholila–Carrileufú–Rivadavia–Verde–Arrayanes–Futalaufquen–Krüger–Frey–Amutui Quimei sequence before following Futaleufú into Chile, traversing Lago Yelcho and continuing down Río Yelcho to the coast. The short eastern side fragment occupies the lower Corintos arrival at Futaleufú.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual selected northern approach follows the mapped Río Tigre around the southern side of the Dos Picos/Campamento mountain setting and enters the western end of Lago Cholila. It is distinct from the Blanco, Villegas and Percey feeders farther north and from Pedregoso near the eastern lake outlet. From Cholila the model follows Carrileufú south to Lago Rivadavia, the Rivadavia river to Lago Verde, and Arrayanes to the northern arm of Lago Futalaufquen. It then uses the western Futalaufquen–Krüger outlet, Río Frey and the eastern portion of Amutui Quimei to reach the Futaleufú outflow. It does not substitute the eastern Futalaufquen–Desaguadero valley or the Menéndez/Cisne and Stange/Chico branches. Below the Corintos junction the selected river turns west across the international boundary, then southwest past the Futaleufú settlement and Azul junction to the Puerto Ramírez bend and southeastern Lago Yelcho entrance. It crosses the long lake toward Puerto Cárdenas and follows Yelcho northwest to the delta/coastal mouth south of Chaitén. The adjacent Espolón/Lonconao, Palena and separate Chaitén river routes are not selected mainstem alternatives.
records.region: Northern Patagonia, Chubut in Argentina and Los Lagos in Chile: the Tigre–Cholila headward corridor, Los Alerces lake chain, Futaleufú valley, Lago Yelcho and the Yelcho coastal mouth south of Chaitén.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river system identity; the selected Tigre, Carrileufú, Rivadavia, Arrayanes, Frey, Futaleufú and Corintos components retain their distinct names and intervening lakes retain their lake identities.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded cartographic correspondence of all five selected fragments using readable official IGN topographic raster mapping of the Argentine course, an original MOP Los Lagos map for the Chilean continuation and coast, and the Argentine national basin account for independent connection and name context. The actual Tigre approach, intervening lakes, western Futalaufquen outlet, reservoir passage, Corintos side stub, international crossing, Lago Yelcho and coastal endpoint were inspected. The connected lake passages and distinct upstream names do not create an unsupported naming scope. Exact formal sources, name-transition vertices, contemporary shorelines and delta-channel allocation are not claimed.

naming_scope_details.headward_component: The selected upper Río Tigre corridor west of Lago Cholila; no precise formal spring, glacier source or longest-natural-headwater claim is made.
naming_scope_details.main_upstream_components: Río Tigre, Río Carrileufú, Río Rivadavia, Río Arrayanes, Río Frey and Río Futaleufú. The Argentine basin account also uses Grande for Futaleufú, confined to that component.
naming_scope_details.lake_components: Lago Cholila, Lago Rivadavia, Lago Verde, Lago Futalaufquen, Lago Krüger, Embalse/Lago Amutui Quimei and Lago Yelcho. Their modeled interior passages do not become rivers named Yelcho.
naming_scope_details.selected_tributary_component: Short lower Río Corintos approach at its Futaleufú junction.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Río Yelcho coastal delta/mouth south of Chaitén.
excluded_inferences: The full modeled mainstem is not asserted to bear the name Río Yelcho or Río Futaleufú.
The selection does not include all named tributaries or complete adjoining lake branches, the whole Corintos basin, the Espolón lake/river branch, or the adjacent Palena basin.
No exact source point, formal naming-transition vertex, present reservoir waterline, precise lake-entry point or modern terminal distributary is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The modeled length is not an official river measurement. Generalized cells simplify mountain turns, lake and reservoir interiors, confluences and the coastal delta. Cartographic connectivity is not a claim of current flow conditions.

records.supported_name_scope: The eastern river corridor is Río Mayer, which flows north in Argentina, turns into Chile and then southwest toward Villa O’Higgins and the northeastern arm of Lago O’Higgins/San Martín. The central lake crossing and the return along the northwestern arm lead to the Pascua outlet and its coastal receiving reach. The selected long line beside the northeastern arm is not fully supported as an actual lake or stream passage by the inspected cartography.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected headward approach is in the upper Mayer drainage east of the northeastern lake arm, in the Sierra de Sangra–General Paz mountain setting. It follows the northeastward upper valley, turns north near the Río Carbón surroundings and continues past the Narváez, Colón and Ñires tributary settings toward the Entrada Mayer border bend. The selected Chilean reach then turns west and southwest past the Lago Briceño/Lago Claro surroundings toward Villa O’Higgins. This is distinct from the separate northern Río Bravo drainage and its Estero Mitchell outlet. The intended lake sequence goes south along the northeastern arm, around the southern end of Península La Florida, and north through the northwestern arm, called Brazo del Desagüe on the MOP sheet. The western terminal river is Pascua, passing the Quetru connection and the Bórquez junction before its delta near Punta Pisagua and Puerto San Carlos in the Calén–Steele fjord setting. The long selected line on the western flank of the northeastern arm crosses mapped land on Península La Florida for a sustained interval; proximity to the correct lake does not by itself establish that exact connection as a water passage.
records.region: Southern Patagonia: western Santa Cruz, Argentina, and southern Aysén, Chile, through the Río Mayer, Villa O’Higgins, Lago O’Higgins/San Martín and coastal Río Pascua setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported representative receiving-river system identity; Río Mayer and the O’Higgins/San Martín lake passages remain distinct components. A substantial modeled connector beside the northeastern lake arm prevents unqualified whole-selection correspondence.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded inspection of all six fragments using complete readable IGN topographic raster coverage, the acquired original MOP Aysén regional sheet, and retained original DGA cartography and prose. The hold is a sustained mapped landward interval along the western flank of the northeastern lake arm, rather than missing coverage, an access failure, a clear lake passage, or the genuine distinction between Mayer and Pascua. No expanded acquisition is required to record the present conservative result. Exact shoreline, bank and river-source positions are not asserted, and the maps alone do not diagnose whether the mismatch originates in model simplification or source cartography.

naming_scope_details.headward_component: Upper Río Mayer drainage; precise formal source and the separate name, if any, of the initial small approach remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.main_upstream_component: Río Mayer in Argentina and Chile.
naming_scope_details.lake_component: Lago O’Higgins/San Martín: northeastern arm, central crossing south of Península La Florida, and northwestern arm/Brazo del Desagüe. The long modeled northeastern-arm connector is not fully supported as a water passage.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Río Pascua and its coastal delta in the Calén–Steele fjord setting.
naming_scope_details.basis_of_hold: The selected northeastern-arm line follows mapped land along Península La Florida for a substantial interval before re-entering the lake. Clear system membership does not establish that exact connector as a continuous mapped watercourse.
excluded_inferences: Do not assert that the full modeled mainstem bears the river name Pascua; Mayer and the lake remain separate components.
Do not substitute Río Bravo, Río Bórquez, Río Ventisquero or a neighboring lake solely because it is nearby.
Do not use the correct receiving lake and river as proof that the long landward connector is an actual channel or lake-center passage.
Do not assign exact river-source points, name-transition vertices, modern shorelines, international-boundary positions or delta-branch allocations from these generalized and partly historical maps.
Do not treat the selected route as the complete Pascua basin or all arms of Lago O’Higgins/San Martín.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The modeled length is not an official river measurement. Regional cartography and generalized cells support named corridors but do not certify exact shoreline or channel coincidence. The sustained northeastern-arm mismatch is retained as scope uncertainty without declaring a definitive engineering defect in either the model or source maps.

records.supported_name_scope: Rivière Corbin is directly labeled along the selected southwestern approach to the lower junction; Rivière Roggan is repeatedly labeled from that junction westward to James Bay. The far-eastern lake-chain component retains narrower unnamed/individually named waterbody scope.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual start is in the eastern small-lake/stream corridor south of the Lac Silly surroundings and north of the separate Kanaaupscow drainage. It proceeds generally west, bows north, then continues southwest through an elongated lake chain north of Lac Julian and south of Lac Burton. The route passes through the Lac Pistinikw setting and turns south then northwest along the mapped Corbin to join Roggan. It then follows only the lower Roggan westward through widened channels to the shore at the Roggan River locality. The separately mapped upper Roggan runs farther south and is not the selected headward route. Rivière au Phoque and Déserclaves lie separately north of the coastal course, and Kapsaouis lies to its south.
records.region: Nord-du-Québec, Canada: northern Eeyou Istchee James Bay lake country and the lower Corbin–Roggan corridor to the eastern James Bay shore at Roggan River.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative lower receiving-river identity; the long selected northern lake-and-stream approach feeds the Corbin component before joining Roggan.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence for all three selected mainstem fragments with original official map pixels. Whole-extent context and overlapping eastern, middle and western enlargements show the lake-chain route, Corbin junction, named lower Roggan and coastal endpoint. Fine island crossings and tiny stream-name transitions are not surveyed; the connected lake/river setting and representative receiving identity are supported without a substantial unviewed interval.

naming_scope_details.headward_component: Northern chain of small lakes and connecting streams, with the farthest small feeders not assigned a uniform river name.
naming_scope_details.upstream_named_component: Rivière Corbin near the lower junction; not extended indiscriminately over every lake in the selected chain.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Lower Rivière Roggan to its James Bay near-mouth setting.
excluded_inferences: Do not rename all upstream lakes and channels Roggan.
Do not substitute the separate southern upper-Roggan course or northern Rivière au Phoque.
No historical naming origin, newly accepted official designation, exact contemporary coastline or surveyed source/transition point is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 298.648 km modeled mainstem length is not an official river-length measurement. Generalization simplifies lake passages, channels, islands and junctions.

records.supported_name_scope: The retained official sources support a completed feature-class and whole-group river-name-scope hold. They do not establish one named natural river corresponding to all seven selected fragments. This does not mean that every nearby marginal stream or glacial watercourse is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: This selection extends broadly westward across the southern Inland Ice, from an eastern interior beginning through several alternating northward and southward bends, before a conspicuous northwestward leg reaches a compact western cluster. The cluster includes the two short lower-mainstem fragments, a southern two-fragment tributary branch and a much shorter northeastern two-fragment branch. The western ending belongs to the southwestern glaciated-margin setting inland of Nuuk / Godthåb and the inner Nuup Kangerlua / Godthåbsfjord country, south of the mapped Isukasia and Ivisartoq locality labels. It is distinct from the southeastern Sermilik and Skjoldungen coastal corridors, and from the more northerly Søndre Strømfjord setting. The selected eastern and middle course is ice interior; the western surroundings include marginal ice, colored exposed bedrock and inland fjord corridors. The historical regional sheet does not resolve a precise ice-front, bedrock/water or shoreline relation for every short fragment or for the final vertex. No endpoint is moved to a nearby named feature.
records.region: Southern Greenland Inland Ice and the southwestern glaciated margin inland of Nuuk / Godthåb and the Nuup Kangerlua / Godthåbsfjord setting.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded source-object correspondence for all three mainstem fragments and all four tributary fragments. The actual retained route and complete selection plot were compared independently with the original geological sheet, readable wide graticule, fresh southwestern regional and marginal enlargements, original Inland Ice legend, and descriptive bulletin pages 64–65. Eastern beginning, long undulating interior course, northwestward approach, short western mainstem and both tributary branches were inspected. The result is a feature-class and naming-scope hold, not an unresolved acquisition or access gap. Positive whole-route natural-river identity evidence would be needed before any later name assignment. Exact present ice-front or marginal-channel positions are outside this historical regional-map determination.

naming_scope_details.selected_mainstem_sequence: Eastern southern-Inland-Ice beginning → northwestward opening → westward interval and southern trough → northwestward rise and central westward interval → southwestern depression → long northwestward approach → short southwestward connector → western marginal bends and actual ending.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: All four selected tributary fragments were inspected: two form the southern westward-then-northwestward branch, and two form the much shorter northeastern westward-then-southwestward branch. Neither branch acquires a river name from its modeled attachment.
naming_scope_details.feature_class_scope: Long southern ice-sheet-interior mainstem plus a compact southwestern marginal cluster. A continuous natural river, outlet glacier or fjord is not established for the full seven-fragment selection.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Regional glaciated-margin, exposed-bedrock and inner-fjord setting inland of Nuuk only. Exact terminal feature, modern glacier front and final ice/land/water boundary remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.nearby_name_scope: Nuuk / Godthåb and Nuup Kangerlua / Godthåbsfjord are geographic context. Isukasia and Ivisartoq are map-locality references north of the terminal region. None is proposed as a river candidate, alias, representative receiving river or assigned endpoint.
naming_scope_details.ice_symbol_scope: Blue ice-surface contours, dashed ice-thickness contours and aeromagnetic lines are not rivers. Sub-ice bedrock contours likewise cannot establish hydrological continuity.
naming_scope_details.length_limit: Modeled inventory display length, not an official or measured natural-river length.
naming_scope_details.name_evidence_limit: Regional historical geological cartography and descriptive glaciology establish setting and naming limits, not a hydronym registry or direct present-day surface/subglacial flow observations.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
